rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a good-quality blastocyst, but it overstates certainty about a dense ICM and uniformly cohesive TE from a single image; the noted stage discrepancy is appropriate, yet some described details are not clearly verifiable.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, prior reproductive history, male factor context, semen parameters, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and generally logical, with the implantation estimate tied to embryo quality and patient modifiers; minor overreach appears in speculation about sperm DNA fragmentation and euploidy likelihood.

SET recommendation and general prognostic framing align well with IVF practice, but recommending PGT-A as highly recommended in a 29-year-old and suggesting ERA/aspirin/heparin without clear indications is more aggressive than guideline-based routine care.

Provides clear next steps for transfer and future evaluation, including SET and targeted workup considerations, though some recommendations would benefit from stronger qualification based on indications.
